Local Tastes
Sancocho
Panama's national dish, a golden chicken soup simmered with yuca, corn on the cob, and culantro, served at family tables and traditional kitchens alike as a cure-all comfort food.
Fonda Lo Que Hay · Mercado de Mariscos · Santa Rita
Ceviche
Corvina or shrimp cured raw in lime juice with onion and cilantro, served ice-cold as a starter across the city and at its freshest straight from the fishing boats.
Mercado de Mariscos · Caleta · Fonda Lo Que Hay
Patacones
Twice-fried green plantain rounds, smashed flat between fryings until crisp outside and starchy within, the standard side dish or bar snack served with a dipping sauce.
Santa Rita · Fonda Lo Que Hay · Mercado de Mariscos
Hojaldras
Panama's fried breakfast dough, crisp outside and pillowy within, eaten alongside fried eggs, white cheese, or a stewed hot dog at any of the city's traditional breakfast counters.
Café Unido · Mercado de Mariscos
Food Delivery
Uber Eats
Foreign number: accepted. — it shares the same Uber account and verification flow as ride-hailing, so a traveler already signed in for rides is signed in here.
Covers Bella Vista, Marbella, San Francisco, and Casco Viejo restaurants well; selection thins out toward the edges of the delivery zone and surge pricing during rain is common.
ubereats.com
PedidosYa
Foreign number: accepted. — the region-wide Delivery Hero signup flow accepts any country code before the SMS step, absorbing Glovo and Appetito24 in Panama.
The most-used delivery app in the country, with the broadest restaurant coverage and grocery/pharmacy delivery alongside food; a Spanish-only interface is the main friction for visitors.
pedidosya.com.pa

Getting Around
Uber
Foreign number: accepted. — the SMS verification code reaches most foreign carriers, though delivery can lag outside North America.
The default choice across the city — Casco Viejo's narrow one-way streets make street hails unreliable, and fares are fixed in-app before pickup, avoiding the haggling some independent taxis expect from visitors.

Heads Up
Miraflores Visitor Center — Time It Right
Ships transit roughly 8–10am and 2–3pm; midday runs quiet, so arrive in the morning window for the best chance of a crossing.
Worth Knowing

A capital that runs on two currencies with one value, and a canal that never closes

Panama's official currency is the Balboa, but no Balboa paper money has ever been printed — US dollar bills are the everyday cash, and Panamanian coins circulate freely alongside identically-sized US coins at the same value. Nobody sorts them at checkout.

Tap water in Panama City is safe to drink straight from the faucet, an exception in the region worth knowing before stocking up on bottled water out of habit.

The famous "Panama hat" is not Panamanian at all — it originated in Ecuador and was popularized after workers wore it during the canal's construction. Panama's own iconic export is Geisha coffee, grown in the highlands around Boquete and served across Casco Viejo's cafés.

Casco Viejo's streets are original colonial cobblestone, uneven in places and occasionally without sidewalks — comfortable closed-toe shoes make a real difference over a full day of walking.

A 10% tip is standard at sit-down restaurants; check the bill first, since some already add a "servicio" charge that covers it.

The canal runs 24 hours a day, every day of the year — a ship transiting at 3am is routine, which is part of why the Miraflores observation decks feel different at each visit.
